clue.text: Finally toasting the party-givers in spirits

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word toasting

parts.note: people who give a party are its hosts

explanation.surface: A last toast raised to the people who threw the party, drunk in spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' looks like drinks to go with the toast, but here it means phantoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits in the supernatural sense are phantoms or spectres of the dead.

clue.text: Jesus knew it as a child — using Tehran A-Z?

definitions.text: Jesus knew it as a child

indicators.note: the question mark with using hints that the letters of the city and the alphabet span are to be rearranged rather than read as they stand

parts.note: an A-Z is a street atlas, giving the letters A and Z

explanation.surface: A question of whether a street map of Tehran would serve Jesus's childhood town.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is a British street-map book; here it just supplies A and Z to mix with TEHRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus grew up in this town in Galilee, according to the Gospels.

clue.text: China's unusual Christmas decorations

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of the word are put in an uncommon order

parts.note: the name of the country with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A remark on the odd Christmas ornaments seen in China.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of China's counts as a letter, giving six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper chains are linked loops hung up as festive decorations.

clue.text: Christmas present drawer acting as a guide

definitions.text: Christmas present drawer acting as a guide

parts.words: Christmas present drawer acting as a guide
parts.note: a drawer here is one who pulls, not a sketcher or a piece of furniture: the reindeer that leads Santa's sleigh of gifts

explanation.surface: Seems to describe an artist or a cabinet of gifts serving as a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' wants to be a chest-of-drawers part or an artist; it means one who draws (pulls) the sleigh full of presents, with a glowing nose to lead the way.
explanation.definitionFit: In the song, the red-nosed reindeer guides Santa's sleigh through fog.

clue.text: It's natural to see a robin around the start of Noel

indicators.note: around suggests the bird's letters are moved about into a new order
the start of asks for the opening letter of the word Noel

explanation.surface: Spotting a robin around Christmas time seems the most natural thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal but here it stirs the letters: ROBIN plus N rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An inborn trait is innate, present from birth rather than learnt.

clue.text: Social activity following high jinks

parts.note: high jinks is read as fun high up on the slopes, so the socialising is what comes after a day on skis

explanation.surface: Looks like partying that follows boisterous fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High jinks' means pranks, but read literally it is fun on the high slopes; the French phrase means 'after skiing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening drinks and socialising at a ski resort once the day's skiing ends.

clue.text: Resolve to be unconscious after the party

indicators.note: after places the word for unconscious behind the word for the party

parts.note: a thrash is informal British slang for a lively party
someone knocked out is out cold

explanation.surface: Determined to be out cold once the party is over.
explanation.walkthrough: THRASH is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash out a problem is to settle it by thorough discussion.

clue.text: Pick off the bird

definitions.meaning: to shoot from a hidden position, choosing targets one by one
a long-billed wading bird of marshes

explanation.definitionFit: A sniper picks off targets; the wader gave its name to that kind of shooting.

clue.text: Turkey — but Marian is cooking with duck!

indicators.note: with here means the round letter is carried inside the cooked mixture
cooking suggests the name and the little word are being worked up into something new

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Christmas kitchen scene: Marian is cooking turkey with a duck as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' is the country, not the bird the surface is roasting; the 'is' after Marian is part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The Asian peninsula of Anatolia makes up most of modern Turkey.

clue.text: One of Santa's reindeer — with a long tail?

definitions.text: One of Santa's reindeer — with a long tail?

parts.words: One of Santa's reindeer — with a long tail?
parts.note: one of the named reindeer shares its name with a heavenly body famed for its long glowing tail

explanation.surface: Asks which of Santa's reindeer has a long tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a reindeer in the Christmas poem and an icy body with a bright streaming tail.

clue.text: A moraliser, not someone like Scrooge, it's said

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letters of the Scrooge figure from the preacher

parts.note: taken as written; that the four letters also run inside moraliser is a coincidence, as the setter's route is removing the skinflint's letters
Scrooge is the classic stingy man, a miser

explanation.surface: A preacher of morals who is no skinflint, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A MISER come out of A MORALISER in order, leaving four.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written, so whatever is said aloud qualifies.

clue.text: Wrongly assert these are Christmas daisies

indicators.note: wrongly signals the letters of the verb are set out incorrectly

explanation.surface: Claims, mistakenly made, about which flowers are Christmas daisies.
explanation.definitionFit: Michaelmas daisies are a kind of aster; the clue gives them a seasonal twist.

clue.text: Swapping presents — the impudence!

indicators.note: swapping suggests the letters of the word trade places

explanation.surface: Someone exchanging their Christmas gifts: how cheeky!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swapping presents' reads as a gift exchange, but it signals the letters of PRESENTS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertness is cheeky boldness, a synonym of impudence.

clue.text: Two presents impossible to locate

parts.note: present in the sense of the current time
present in the sense of being in this place

explanation.surface: Two Christmas gifts that have gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presents' are not gifts but two senses of 'present': at this time, and in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nowhere to be found cannot be located anywhere.

clue.text: Pretty useless object on the tree?

definitions.text: Pretty useless object on the tree?

parts.words: Pretty useless object on the tree?
parts.note: something pretty but serving no use, hung on the Christmas tree as a bauble

explanation.surface: A grumble about something fairly pointless sitting on the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty useless' reads as 'fairly pointless', but it means attractive and decorative only.
explanation.definitionFit: A bauble hung on the Christmas tree is a decoration valued only for looks.

clue.text: Christmas fare always includes traditional sort of ale

indicators.note: includes shows the letters sit inside the run of words before it

explanation.surface: Seasonal food and drink always comes with a traditional beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans 'faRE ALways'.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is the British term for traditionally brewed, cask-conditioned beer.

clue.text: A boy acquiring djinn, oddly

parts.note: a boy is a lad

indicators.note: oddly asks for the first, third and fifth letters of the word djinn

explanation.surface: A young lad comes by a genie in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the pantomime hero who acquires a genie from a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy of the Arabian Nights tale who gains a genie by rubbing a lamp.

clue.text: Give one an order: "Put up the ornaments!"

definitions.meaning: to award someone a medal or membership of an order of chivalry
to adorn a room with festive trimmings

explanation.definitionFit: Both bestowing an honour on a person and adorning a room with trimmings.

clue.text: Old man's cracking nuts

indicators.note: cracking suggests the words are broken apart and reassembled

parts.note: the phrase with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: An old man is busy cracking Christmas nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' sits naturally with nuts but signals the rearrangement; the 's counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Almonds are edible seeds commonly eaten as nuts.

clue.text: Winter dance thrown for enjoyment?

definitions.meaning: a formal dance held in the snowy season
a packed lump of snow hurled in play

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a winter ball; as one, the icy missile kids throw.

clue.text: Property of the Magi

parts.note: the Magi are the three wise men, and property means a quality rather than belongings

explanation.surface: Looks like asking what the three kings owned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Property' suggests their gifts or belongings; it means a characteristic, and the Magi are called wise men.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being wise, the trait for which the Magi are known.

clue.text: Blooming choir spoilt start of "Deck The Halls"

indicators.note: spoilt suggests the singers' word is messed up into a new order
start of asks for the opening letter of the carol's first word

explanation.surface: A carol choir ruins the opening of a famous Christmas song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' seems a mild British curse aimed at the choir, but it defines a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This exotic flower is a bloom, so the definition works as 'one blooming'.

clue.text: Remove top of boxes to reveal presents

indicators.note: remove top of tells us to drop the first letter of the chests

parts.note: coffers are strong boxes for valuables

explanation.surface: Lift the lids off the boxes to see the Christmas gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presents' is a verb here, meaning puts forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer something is to present it, as a verb in the third person.

clue.text: In the freezer find diamonds, a Christmas present

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
a Christmas box is a seasonal gift or tip, traditionally given on Boxing Day

explanation.surface: Diamonds tucked away in the freezer as a Christmas gift.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas box is the traditional British seasonal tip given to tradespeople.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is an old name for a refrigerator or freezer compartment.

clue.text: Gather it's what people may go to church at Christmas for

definitions.text: it's what people may go to church at Christmas for
definitions.meaning: a religious service such as midnight Mass, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate things together; split into two words it names a church service.

clue.text: Woollen scarf worn in cold weather — Job's one wasn't much help!

definitions.text: Woollen scarf worn in cold weather

definitions.meaning: Job's friends in the Bible offered poor consolation, giving the phrase Job's consoler

explanation.definitionFit: Both an old word for a warm muffler and one who consoles; Job's were famously useless.

clue.text: Note down new present

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: new suggests the word down is made afresh in another order

explanation.surface: An instruction to jot down a fresh Christmas gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note down' reads as 'write', but splits into a musical note and a word to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give or bestow, a verb sense of present.

clue.text: Love helping after a party

indicators.note: after places the portion behind the party

parts.note: a do is an informal party
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: Fond feelings for a second helping once the party is over.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and worship, a near synonym.
